resources.string: World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King
Starts your %1$s realm on this phone.
Starts your %1$s realm and the game, on this phone.
Starts your %1$s realm on this phone. The world server starts once it has the server data.
The world server needs data made from your 3.3.5a client: make it here from the client, or import the server-data.zip made on a PC.
This build of the app has no server in it. Install a release from GitHub.
From a PC on this Wi-Fi
Two realms live on this phone and run one at a time, with the same accounts. Each has its own characters, world and settings: nothing you do on one changes the other.
Azeroth as ChromieCraft runs it: from level 1, the content opening bracket by bracket.
Northrend\'s story from level 10, with Moratari and the Infinite Dragonflight: every chapter at your level, quicker levels, Bronze to earn and spend, and the Infinite Bazaar.
%1$s chosen. The server stops now; Press start starts %1$s.
The first start of Wrath Remix makes its own databases (a few minutes, once).
To play on this phone, add your 3.3.5a client in Game files. A PC\'s 3.3.5a client on this Wi-Fi can play on the realm too: see Server.
Running, without the world server (no server data yet)
Open the app to see why.
The first start fills in the world: every creature, quest and item. It takes a few minutes, once.
Taking out what the modules you took out put in the world…
A module that\'s no longer in your realm leaves what it added in the world database, so the world database is made again without it (a few minutes). Your characters stay.
The custom races are gone from the app: the world database is made again without them (a few minutes, once). Characters made with them stay, out of the character list.
The app\'s storage is at %1$s, not where the server expects it. The server only runs for the phone\'s main user, not in a second user or a work profile.
The server\'s setup failed (%1$s ended with %2$d).
The server\'s setup took too long (%1$s didn\'t finish).
The world server stopped while loading (code %1$d).
The world server took more than 30 minutes to load.

On a PC on the same Wi-Fi, in your 3.3.5a client's folder, open Data\enUS\realmlist.wtf and make its line

set realmlist %1$s

then start Wow.exe and log in with one of your accounts. The phone has to stay on this Wi-Fi with the server running.
Connect the phone to Wi-Fi to play on the realm from a PC.
Let the app run without battery restrictions, so Android doesn\'t stop the server with the screen off.
Deletes the databases: accounts, characters and the world. The next start makes them again, as new. Stop the server first. Your client, server data and settings stay.

Your own copy of the 3.3.5a (12340) client, enUS, about 17 GB: pick its folder (the one with Wow.exe and Data in it), or a zip of it. Move it onto the phone first: files in cloud folders can\'t be read this way. The app keeps its own copy, and checks it\'s build 12340.

The world server needs dbc and maps from the client; vmaps add line of sight, and mmaps pathfinding, which creatures and bots need to move well. Download them ready-made, or make them from your client on this phone or on a PC.

AzerothCore\'s ready-made server data for 3.3.5a, all five folders, in the version this server is built for: a %1$s download that unpacks to %2$s. It doesn\'t need your client. Best on Wi-Fi; if it stops, it carries on from where it got to.
From the client added above. dbc, maps and vmaps take minutes; mmaps an hour or more, with the phone getting warm. It carries on with the app in the background.

Faster. Download WarcraftServerData-windows.zip from the same GitHub release as the app, unzip it on the PC, and drag your client\'s folder onto extract-server-data.bat. Copy the server-data.zip it makes to the phone, then import it here.
Downloading the Worgen and Goblin starting areas
Downloading the Worgen and Goblin starting areas… %1$d%%
Unpacking the Worgen and Goblin starting areas… %1$d%%
The Worgen and Goblin starting areas are in. New Worgen start in Gilneas, new Goblins in Kezan, from the realm\'s next start.
Not enough free space for the starting areas: %1$d MB more needed.
The server data is downloaded. Start the server to load the world.
The download stopped (%1$s). Try again: it carries on from where it got to.
The download came out damaged, and was deleted. Try again.
Making the server data… part %1$d of %2$d
The server data is made. Start the server to load the world.
The server data is imported. Start the server to load the world.
You can leave the app: this carries on, and its notification shows how far it is.
Stopped before the end: nothing was changed.
It didn\'t work. Open the app to see why.
Couldn\'t read %1$s. If it\'s in a cloud folder, move it to the phone first.
Couldn\'t write to the app\'s storage.
The zip is damaged or packed in a way the app can\'t read (%1$s).
Not enough free space: this needs %1$s and the phone has %2$s free.
There\'s no World of Warcraft client in it: a client folder has Wow.exe next to a Data folder with common.MPQ.
This client is version %1$s. The server is for 3.3.5a, build 12340 (3.3.5.12340).
There\'s no server data in that zip (dbc, maps, vmaps, mmaps folders).
The server data is still missing dbc or maps.
The accounts are in the server\'s database: start the server to see and change them.
No accounts yet. Make one to log in with.
Every GM command, in the game\'s chat (.help lists them)
Names: 3 to 16 letters and digits. Passwords: 4 to 16 characters, no spaces. The game ignores upper and lower case in both.
Account names are 3 to 16 letters and digits.
Passwords are 4 to 16 characters, without spaces.
There\'s already an account with that name.
The app\'s icon on the home screen. Your launcher may take a moment to show the new one, and removes shortcuts of the old one.
%1$s is available. You have %2$s.\n\nDownload it (%3$s) and install it now? The server stops first; your accounts, characters and files stay.
This build doesn\'t know where its updates are published. Builds from GitHub Actions do.
GitHub didn\'t let the app see the releases (error %1$d). If the repository is private, the build needs an update token (see Updates in the README).
GitHub answered with error %1$d. Try again later.
Can\'t reach GitHub. Check your internet connection and try again.
The downloaded file isn\'t an update for this app.
Android needs your permission for %1$s to install its updates. Turn on \"Allow from this source\", then come back.
The first time only: Wine, Box64 and the graphics drivers, which run the Windows game on this phone.
The 3.3.5a client isn\'t in the app: add it in Game files.
Couldn\'t install the game\'s Windows. Is there space on the phone?
Couldn\'t set up the game\'s Windows.
The server was stopped before the realm was up.
The realm has no world yet: it needs the server data (Game files).
Make your game account first (Accounts): the game\'s login screen asks for it.
Leaving closes the game. Log out in it first (Escape → Log Out) so your character leaves the world cleanly.
That zip has no Character folder of textures.
The game\'s resolution, for the screen the phone is showing now (a Fold\'s inside or outside). It takes effect the next time the game starts. Fewer pixels run smoother and keep the phone cooler.

HD textures and models for the game, from ChromieCraft\'s downloads page. Only the patch files are downloaded, into your client; picking Off takes them out again. They take effect the next time the game starts. The game runs as a copy of Wow.exe that may use 4 GB of memory (your Wow.exe stays as it is).
ChromieCraft\'s HD patch: characters, creatures and mounts, the world\'s and cities\' textures, sunlight. About 3.4 GB to download.
The community HD client\'s look: HD characters, models and NPCs, the world\'s textures, spells, water, sky, music and loading screens. About 7.6 GB to download.
Your client is changed. It takes effect the next time the game starts.
Your Wow.exe isn\'t the 3.3.5a (12340) one these changes are made for (%1$s).
Add your 3.3.5a client first (Game files): add-ons go in it.
No add-ons yet. Find some in Browse, or import a zip.
There\'s no add-on in that zip (no .toc file).
made for another version of the game
Add-ons from warperia.com. An install waits the few seconds the site asks of free downloads, then goes into your client by itself.
Add-ons load the next time the game starts (or type /reload in the game). A turned-off one stays on the phone without loading.
Typed into the game\'s text box
⌫, or the keyboard\'s Backspace with this box empty, deletes a letter in the game\'s box.
Keeps the password on this phone (Accounts turns it off)
Log in automatically: the game types this account\'s password at the login screen by itself. The password stays on this phone, in the app\'s own storage.
The game logs in with this account by itself. Its password is kept on this phone.
%1$s logs in automatically from now on
Needs a build from this repository\'s releases
Your realm is built: put it in
This build of the app can\'t build a realm (a build made on a PC). The builds on this repository\'s releases can.
Modules from github.com/topics/azerothcore-module. Each is someone\'s own code: they change the realm itself.

A module is code built into the realm\'s world server. Added ones come in when the realm is built again (Your realm), at the branch\'s newest commit. Its README says what it needs: some want settings (files/etc/modules), a client patch or a version of AzerothCore other than ChromieCraft\'s.

The realm\'s world server is built with its modules in it, so a realm with yours is built again: by this app\'s repository on GitHub (its workflow build-warcraft-modules.yml: about 20 minutes, longer with many modules), from this version\'s own release, then tested the way the app\'s own realm is (the world server started, a character taken into the world). The app then downloads it and puts it in place of the realm, which stops for it. Characters, accounts, bots and settings stay; each module\'s database changes are made at the realm\'s next start.
The app\'s own realm: the one with your modules was built for an earlier version of the app. Build it again for this one.
Put the app\'s own realm back
Add modules in Browse, then build the realm with them here.
Waiting for GitHub to start the build…
With %1$s · asked for %2$s. It carries on with the app closed; the app looks again when it opens.
Built and tested. Put it in to play with it.
The realm stops while it goes in; start it again after.
The build failed at: %1$s. Its log is on GitHub; a module may not build with this realm\'s AzerothCore.
Built for an earlier version of the app: build it again for this one.
GitHub needs your token to start a build: a fine-grained token for this app\'s repository.
Your GitHub token is in (kept in this app only).

On github.com: Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens → Fine-grained tokens → Generate new token. Repository access: only %1$s. Permissions: Actions, read and write; and Issues, read and write, for the game\'s Report Time Anomaly to send its reports unseen. Paste it here: it\'s checked with GitHub, then kept in this app\'s own storage and sent to GitHub alone.
Time anomaly reported on GitHub: issue #%1$d.
%1$s went home to ChromieCraft. The server is starting again there: press start to log in, in your side\'s capital.
Your time anomaly report is open on GitHub: send it from there.
Your time anomaly report couldn\'t open: no browser on this phone.
Your time anomaly report will go to GitHub once the phone is online.

The game\'s crash report is open on GitHub: send it from there.
The game\'s crash report couldn\'t open: no browser on this phone.

The app\'s failure report is open on GitHub: send it from there.
The app\'s failure report couldn\'t open: no browser on this phone.
The app\'s failure report will go to GitHub once the phone is online.
The game\'s crash report will go to GitHub once the phone is online.

The release %2$s has no %1$s any more (it keeps the last three builds): build it again.
That realm isn\'t on the phone any more: build it again.
Built without %1$s: it doesn\'t compile with this realm\'s AzerothCore (it was written for another one). Remove it from your modules, or look for an up-to-date fork of it.
Build it again for this version

Each realm you put in is kept on the phone, so you can swap between them and the app\'s own realm in a minute or two, without building again. The world database follows: what a module taken out added there goes at the realm\'s next start (a few minutes). Characters stay.
Built for an earlier version of the app: build it again to use it.
The realm is changed. It runs at its next start.
